headline: Morgan Stanley estimates that AI spending by big tech and cloud firms will reach about $1.58 trillion in 2027 once leased data centres are counted.
score_reason: Large bank research with a new way of counting AI spending and a financing warning; relayed by an aggregator and not independently confirmed.
importance_line: Investors in tech shares and the banks and funds lending to AI builders are affected first, since leases hide part of the spending bill from company guidance, but this is one bank's forecast and its 25% to 50% return estimate is an assumption not yet proven.
source: BigGo Finance, citing Morgan Stanley research
summary: BigGo Finance, reporting Morgan Stanley research, says the bank estimates AI computing investment by the giant cloud companies and newer cloud firms will reach about $1.58 trillion in 2027, about 14% more than the usual measure, because data-centre leases are not counted as capital spending. Morgan Stanley also sees 2027 as the year with the largest cash shortfall and says lower-rated borrowers such as Oracle are far more exposed to rising borrowing costs than Amazon, Meta, Google and Microsoft.
notes: Read on BigGo Finance, an aggregator that reports the Morgan Stanley note; the note itself was not seen and the article gives no date for it. The article's $700 billion 2026-to-2027 increase does not match its own totals and was left out.
